item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani to return from IL Wednesday, but Dodgers still have unanswered questions in final week
- Click here to listen to this article
-
The Dodgers have less than a week left of the regular season to round into playoff form. And their roster moves this series reflect that time crunch.
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday afternoon that Shohei Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) was on track to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list on Wednesday. Ohtani is feeling “considerably” better than he was before the IL stint, according to Roberts.
“I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or a nine right now,” Roberts said before eight pitchers led the Dodgers’ 7-0 win against the San Diego Padres.
On Tuesday, they returned two other important postseason pieces, reinstating center fielder Andy Pages (fractured left hand) and right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) from the injured list.
In corresponding moves, the Dodgers optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliézer Alfonzo to triple-A Oklahoma City.
Sasaki took the fourth inning of the bullpen game and threw scoreless ball. He gave up a pair of singles, but his fastball had a little extra life in the short stint, averaging 98.7 mph and topping out at 101.7.
Pages went 0 for 2 but reached base twice, on a hit by pitch and a walk.
Even as players return, however, there are still questions the Dodgers have to answer in the last week of the season:
Where will Ohtani hit?
At least at first, Roberts plans to write Ohtani in at the top of the order, per usual. But shortstop Mookie Betts has entered the conversation.
“Certainly versus right-handed pitching [Ohtani] will be there,” Roberts said. “I do think I should think through the Mookie versus left situation, but I have to think about the entire lineup structure.”
Ohtani has hit leadoff in every game he’s started this year. But he hit No. 2 in 79 games the two previous seasons combined.
Even without Ohtani, the Dodgers lineup has been clicking. On Tuesday, Tommy Edman hit his second home run in as many games, and Will Smith homered for the third time in four days.
Is the rotation healthy?
Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, who exited his start last week with left groin tightness, threw a bullpen on Tuesday. He’s scheduled for one final regular-season start Saturday, Roberts said.
That means all four of the Dodgers’ projected playoff starters are lined up to pitch this Wednesday through Saturday, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow on the mound for the last two games against the Padres, and Tarik Skubal and Snell in the first two games in San Francisco.
Who is the closer?
In short, it could change by the day.
“In a perfect world, as we all know the world’s not perfect, I would love [a set closer],” Roberts said. “I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner [Scott] to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there. Because you just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.
“Those are things that you have to kind of toil with, and those are always good things for people to debate. Right now I don’t see a one-person closer.”
Sasaki stepped into that role last year. It’s unclear exactly how Roberts will use him this time around, but Roberts said he could be an option, depending on how he pitches coming off the IL.
“Last year it was one of those things where it was a situation of need, as far as where we were at with performance and health and guys,” Roberts said. “He filled that role admirably.”
Who gets the last bench spot?
The battle to serve as the left-handed bat off the bench in the postseason has come down to rookie Josue De Paula and injured catcher Dalton Rushing (right flexor strain). But with Rushing still on the IL, De Paula appears to have an edge.
Don’t read too much into the Dodgers’ corresponding move for Ohtani on Wednesday. If they option De Paula 10 days out from the first game of the National League Division Series, he can still be included on the roster.
The Dodgers will have to make another roster move later in the week, when they plan to activate Rushing. If they option a player to make room for Rushing, that player would only be eligible for the start of the NLDS as the corresponding transaction for an IL move.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES -- Roki Sasaki llamó la atención cuando pasó al bullpen durante la marcha del año pasado hacia el bicampeonato. Volverá a desempeñar ese papel en los últimos días de esta temporada regular y posiblemente vuelva a estar entre las opciones para cerrar juegos.
Sasaki fue activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días antes de la victoria por 7-0 sobre los Padres la noche del martes, como parte de una serie de movimientos que también incluyeron el regreso del cubano Andy Pagés de la lista de lesionados y el envío de Emmet Sheehan y el venezolano Eliezer Alfonzo a Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sasaki lanzó por última vez el 26 de agosto, cuando una ampolla en el dedo medio de la mano derecha puso fin prematuramente a su apertura contra los Bravos.
En su segunda temporada en Grandes Ligas, Sasaki se acercaba cada vez más a la versión de sí mismo que fue un fenómeno en la Liga Japonesa de Béisbol Profesional (NPB, por sus siglas en inglés). Tuvo marca de 5-5 con efectividad de 4.60 en 23 aperturas, pero esos números no cuentan toda la historia. Con un repertorio más amplio, que incluye un nuevo splitter, y una mayor velocidad en su recta, Sasaki tuvo su mejor tramo sostenido como abridor en Grandes Ligas, registrando efectividad de 2.63 en siete aperturas antes de lidiar con la ampolla.
“Emocionado de tener a Roki de vuelta”, dijo el manager Dave Roberts. “Está entusiasmado con este rol. Creo que puede tener un gran impacto, como lo tuvo el año pasado”.
En su regreso al bullpen el martes, Sasaki ponchó a dos en un cuarto inning en blanco, pese a permitir un par de sencillos con dos outs. Generó cuatro swings fallidos, incluidos dos en igual número de swings contra su splitter, y promedió 98.7 mph con las ocho rectas que lanzó, ligeramente por encima de su promedio de 97.8 mph esta temporada.
Los Dodgers mejoraron su récord a 97-60 después de que su juego de bullpen terminara en blanqueada. Están cinco juegos por delante de los Bravos en la lucha por el segundo mejor récord de la Liga Nacional y a uno de los Cerveceros, líderes del circuito y dueños del criterio de desempate entre ambos.
El año pasado, el traslado de Sasaki al relevo fue una decisión sin precedentes. Después de un comienzo por debajo de las expectativas en su temporada de novato y de perderse más de cuatro meses por una lesión en el hombro, la única oportunidad de Sasaki de contribuir con los Dodgers en la postemporada era pasar al bullpen.
Sasaki no sólo contribuyó, sino que se convirtió en el cerrador de los Dodgers en la postemporada, permitiendo apenas una carrera limpia en 10.2 innings, para efectividad de 0.84. La confianza que adquirió al conseguir resultados en Grandes Ligas, bajo la máxima presión, impulsó el regreso del derecho de 24 años a la rotación y su posterior despegue a mitad de esta temporada.
Actualmente, los Dodgers no cuentan con un cerrador fijo, ya que el boricua Edwin Díaz está lanzando en situaciones de baja presión en medio de sus dificultades a lo largo de la temporada, mientras busca ganarse un puesto en el bullpen para la postemporada. Díaz ponchó a dos en un quinto inning perfecto la noche del martes, su tercera presentación sin permitir carreras desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados.
Ha pasado mucho tiempo desde que Sasaki lanzó como relevista, pero si logra mostrarle lo suficiente a Roberts durante la última semana antes de la postemporada, podría convertirse en una opción para situaciones de salvamento.
“Creo que sin duda es una opción”, dijo Roberts. “Probablemente mucho dependerá de cómo lance esta noche. Seguramente tendrá una o dos presentaciones cortas más antes de que termine la temporada”.
Con Díaz perdiendo tiempo de juego por lesiones en el codo y el cuello, además de no lanzar bien cuando estuvo saludable, el zurdo Tanner Scott ha recibido la mayoría de las oportunidades de salvamento. Scott lidera a los Dodgers con 23 rescates, pero también ha desperdiciado cuatro oportunidades, incluidas dos desde comienzos de septiembre.
Scott todavía podría ser la mejor opción para cerrar los juegos, pero Sasaki podría complementarlo desde el lado derecho, algo importante debido a que el derecho venezolano Edgardo Henríquez estará fuera por el resto de la temporada regular debido a una distensión en la parte baja de la espalda. Se espera que regrese durante la postemporada.
Aunque a Roberts le gustaría contar con un cerrador en la postemporada, reconoció que es más probable que maneje el bullpen según los enfrentamientos. En esta época del año, algunas de las situaciones de mayor presión se presentan antes del noveno inning, por lo que tener varias opciones le permitiría utilizar a sus mejores relevistas en los momentos más convenientes.
“Creo que si hay una oportunidad, por ejemplo, de que Tanner lance un inning de alta presión en el séptimo u octavo, es difícil dejarla pasar si es la mejor opción en ese momento”, dijo Roberts. “Porque simplemente no sabes cómo se va a presentar el noveno inning”.

LOS ANGELES -- Roki Sasaki opened eyes when he moved to the bullpen for last year's run to back-to-back championships. He'll reprise that role in the final days of this regular season -- and possibly be in the mix to close out games once again.
Sasaki was activated from the 15-day injured list ahead of Tuesday night's series opener against the Padres amid a flurry of moves that also saw Andy Pages return from the IL and Emmet Sheehan and Eliezer Alfonzo get optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sasaki last pitched on Aug. 26, when a blister on his right middle finger brought his start against the Braves to a premature end.
In his second Major League season, Sasaki was steadily growing closer to resembling the version of himself who was a phenom in Nippon Professional Baseball. He went 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA through 23 starts, but those numbers don't tell the full story. Working with an expanded pitch mix, including a new splitter, and increased fastball velocity, Sasaki put together his best sustained stretch as an MLB starter, recording a 2.63 ERA through seven starts before dealing with the blister.
"Excited to see Roki back," manager Dave Roberts said. "He's looking forward to this role. I think he can be very impactful, as it was last year."
In his return to the bullpen on Tuesday, Sasaki was available to pitch multiple innings. He will likely get a couple of additional relief appearances in the final five games of the regular season.
Last year, Sasaki's shift to relief was an unprecedented move. After underperforming to begin his rookie season and then missing more than four months with a shoulder injury, Sasaki's only chance to contribute to the Dodgers in the postseason was to move to the 'pen.
Sasaki didn't just contribute -- he became the Dodgers' postseason closer, allowing just one earned run in 10 2/3 innings (0.84 ERA). The confidence he gained from getting results at the big league level, with the stakes as high as could be, fueled the 24-year-old right-hander's return to the rotation and eventual midseason breakout this year.
The Dodgers are currently working without a set closer, as Edwin Díaz is pitching in low leverage amid his season-long struggles as he looks to earn a role in the postseason bullpen. It has been a long time since Sasaki has pitched in relief, but if he can show Roberts enough in the final week before the postseason, he could very well be an option in save situations.
"I think it's certainly an option," Roberts said. "A lot of it, probably, is contingent on how he throws here tonight. He'll probably get another one or two shorter stints before the season's end."
With Díaz missing time with elbow and neck injuries -- and not pitching well when healthy -- left-hander Tanner Scott has gotten the bulk of save opportunities. Scott leads the Dodgers with 23 saves, but he's also blown four saves, including two since the start of September.
Scott may still be the best option to close out games, but Sasaki could complement him from the right-hand side, which is important with leverage righty Edgardo Henriquez out for the rest of the regular season with a lower back strain (he is expected back during the postseason).
While Roberts would like to have a closer in the postseason, he acknowledged that it's more likely that he will play the matchups. At this time of year, some of the highest-leverage situations take place before the ninth inning, so having multiple options would free up Roberts to use his best relievers in the lanes that make sense.
"I think if there's an opportunity, for example, for Tanner to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it's just hard to pass that up if he's the best option right there," Roberts said. "Because you just don't know where the ninth inning is going to be."

The Los Angeles Dodgers activated a pair of key contributors in advance of a marquee series against the San Diego Padres, bringing back center fielder Andy Pages and right-hander Roki Sasaki from the injured list.
In corresponding moves, right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Pages, 25, has not played since Aug. 21, when he was hit by a pitch on the left hand from Pittsburgh Pirates right-hander Bubba Chandler. An All-Star for the first time this season, Pages was batting .272 with 21 home runs and 80 RBIs in 128 games.
Sasaki, 24, last pitched Aug. 26 when he developed a blister on his right middle finger in an outing against the Atlanta Braves. He is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA in 23 outings (all starts) this season and is scheduled to make an abbreviated appearance Tuesday.
Sheehan, 26, started the season in the Los Angeles rotation, was sent down in early August amid ongoing struggles and has returned for three outings this month where he recorded 24 strikeouts over 17 innings. He is 5-8 with a 4.57 ERA in 23 appearances (22 starts) this season.
Sheehan and Sasaki both are projected to have a bullpen role for the Dodgers in the playoffs, according to manager Dave Roberts.
Alfonzo, 26, made his major league debut in July and is batting .179 with four RBIs in 13 career games.
While the Dodgers enter Tuesday's play with a magic number of three to clinch a bye into a National League Division Series matchup, the Padres have a magic number of two to clinch a wild-card spot and a team-record third consecutive playoff appearance.
Also on Tuesday, the Dodgers sold Ryan Ward's contract to the Chunichi Dragons in Japan, according to multiple reports. A longtime minor leaguer, the 28-year-old Ward made his major league debut this season and hit three home runs in 20 games. The former Pacific Coast League MVP was designated for assignment last week.

He was signed by the Dodgers as an international free agent on March 1, 2018 out of La Habana, Cuba.
Sasaki, 24, has been on the injured list since August 27 with a blister on his right middle finger. In his second full season with the Dodgers, he is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA, including a 2-0 record with a 3.05 ERA since the All-Star break. He has made 33 Major League appearances in his career, posting a 6-6 mark with a 4.57 ERA and 145 strikeouts in 155.2 innings. Sheehan, 26, pitched 5.1 scoreless innings on Sunday against the Giants. He is 5-8 and a 4.57 ERA with the Dodgers in 2026, racking up 132 strikeouts in 112.1 innings. He is in his third season with the Dodgers, recording a 4.13 ERA with a 15-12 record in 51 games (45 starts). He was drafted by the Dodgers in the sixth round of the 2021 First Year Player Draft out of Boston College.
Alfonzo, 26, has played in 13 games for the Dodgers this season, batting .179 with two doubles and four RBI. He was batting .302 with two homers and 25 RBI with Triple-A Oklahoma City this season. He has appeared in 598 minor league games, batting .283 with 33 homers and 291 RBI. He signed with the Dodgers as a minor league free agent on November 17, 2025.

LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list.
Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger.
Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
Pages was an All-Star starter this season, and when he got hurt was tied with Yoshinobu Yamamoto for second-highest FanGraphs WAR (3.9) on the team, behind only Shohei Ohtani. By Baseball Reference WAR, Pages is still third on the team now at 5.4, trailing only Ohtani and Yamamoto. That’ll happen with a .272/.338/.458 batting line with a 118 wRC+ combined with plus-defense in center field.
Before getting hit by an errant fastball on August 21, Pages started 125 of the Dodgers’ 129 games, and led the team in plate appearances (550) at the time. Pages and Ohtani are still tied for the Dodgers’ lead with 80 runs batted in. With Pages out, Alek Thomas was first called up to start six games in center field, followed by Tommy Edman starting 17 games, plus three starts by Alex Call and one by Kiké Hernández.
With Edman moving to the outfield and once Thomas was optioned, Miguel Rojas (10) and Alex Freeland (eight) have covered all but one of the starts at second base in September.
Sasaki struggled earlier in the season, but improved as the season progressed. He has a streak of six straight starts with no more than two runs allowed until his blister start in Atlanta. On the season, Sasaki has a 4.46 ERA and 4.42 xERA, but since July 8 he’s down to a 3.25 ERA and 3.76 xERA in eight starts.
With Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and Tyler Glasnow set for the postseason rotation, the Dodgers will see over the next two weeks if Blake Snell will be hampered by his left groin discomfort, and will have Sheehan at the ready. That allows them to use Sasaki in relief, as they did last postseason out of necessity.
“I could see multiples [innings], but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings,” manager Dave Roberts said on Sunday.
Last season was a different situation for Sasaki, who struggled mightily as a starter and spend four months on the injured list before returning in the final week of the regular season. There was no room in the rotation, so he pitched in relief in the postseason. He wasn’t dominant — only six strikeouts among his 43 batters faced, with five walks — but he was effective, allowing only one run over nine appearances and 10 2/3 innings, the highlight his perfect three innings of relief in the Dodgers’ NLDS Game 4 clincher over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Sasaki saved three games last postseason. Roberts said Sasaki probably wouldn’t get an opportunity in a save situation right away this week, but it could progress to that by the postseason.
“I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably starting a clean inning,” Roberts said. “He’s done it, he’s really good. He’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff. And you really just need four starters. So we’re in a good spot there, for now.”
Sheehan has been fantastic of late, allowing only one run in three starts for the Dodgers over the previous two weeks, with 24 strikeouts in 17 innings. The plan for Sheehan is to start on Saturday for Oklahoma City should the Comets advance to the Triple-A championship game.
Alfonzo was back with the Dodgers since September 6 when Dalton Rushing was placed on the injured list with elbow soreness. In the 14 games since, Alfonzo played only once, pinch-hitting as the designated hitter at the end of a 14-1 blowout of the Cincinnati Reds. He struck out.
Alfonzo made his major league debut against the Padres on July 5, and started nine games behind the plate. He had five hits in 28 at-bats with three doubles and four runs batted in.

The Los Angeles Dodgers activated Andy Pages from the 10-day injured list and optioned Eliezer Alfonzo to Triple-A Oklahoma City. The move was made during the off day on Monday, but the Dodgers did not officially announce it at the time.
In addition, Roki Sasaki was also activated while Emmet Sheehan was optioned.
The Dodgers first recalled Alfonzo when Dalton Rushing was placed on the IL on Sept. 6. During his second stint with the club, Alfonzo only received one at-bat, which came against the Cincinnati Reds on Sept. 9 when he struck out.
Alfonzo was the third catcher on the roster, which Dodgers manager Dave Roberts explained was to allow the club to more freely use Will Smith and Hunter Feduccia as pinch-hitters when they didn’t start.
The Dodgers also did not need to make a 40-man roster move to call up Alfonzo, which likely played into their decision.
The 26-year-old has appeared in 13 total games this season, making his MLB debut and batting .179/.179/.250 with four RBI and three runs scored in 28 plate appearances. In Oklahoma City, he was hitting .302/.378/.409 in 256 plate appearances.
Pages is back with the Dodgers for the first time in a month after he landed on the IL with a left hand fracture on Aug. 22.
Pages suffered the injury when he was hit by a pitch from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler. The 26-year-old underwent surgery shortly after to insert a compression screw in his hand to speed up the healing process.
Pages did not go on a rehab assignment before returning, but did workouts at Dodger Stadium, which included hitting on the field, running the bases, and doing outfield drills.
That makes this stretch of six games important for Pages to face live pitching and get as many at-bats as possible to prepare for the postseason. But even with that in mind, the Dodgers also have to be cautious about building him back up and not overworking him after a month of not playing.
“So we have obviously, assuming he gets back on Tuesday, then there’s six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive,” Roberts explained.
“So I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. So it is going to be a balancing act, and just keeping a keen eye on Andy for sure.”
Pages is batting .272/.338/.458 with 25 doubles, 21 home runs, 80 RBI and 72 runs scored this season. He has also been among the top defensive players in MLB.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are pacing toward having a first-round bye, avoiding the NL Wild Card round, and it would seem they are getting healthy at just the right time. The expectation in recent weeks was that Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki would return before the end of the regular season, and the Dodgers quietly revealed the roster moves to map everything out.
Updating their transaction log overnight, the Dodgers have reinstated Pages and Sasaki from the IL, and optioned Emmet Sheehan and Eliezer Alfonzo to the minors. With Ohtani eligible to be reinstated from the IL on Wednesday, the expectation is that Alex Freeland will be the corresponding move.
For Ohtani and Pages, the goal was simply having them back before the start of the playoffs. They now have a runway to shake off the rust over these next handful of games, before likely having next week off before playing in the NLDS.
Circumstances are a little more dire for Sasaki, who hasn't secured a spot on LA's playoff roster. Dave Roberts has already confirmed that Sasaki will be used out of the bullpen upon his return, and it goes to one of the biggest questions facing the Dodgers ahead of the playoffs.
The Dodgers are getting healthy just in time, but there are still answers needed
The Dodgers need to find answers in the bullpen. Ironically, the stage is set for Sasaki to repeat a similar shift he made last season. While the Dodgers have been adamant that Sasaki's future is as a starting pitcher, he was used as a quasi-finisher during the playoffs last year, and thrived.
Considering the questions surrounding Edwin Diaz and Edgardo Henriquez currently dealing with an injury, Sasaki once again becoming an effective high-leverage option for the Dodgers would be a major development for the playoffs.
The story of the Dodgers since the trade deadline has been that they are leaking oil. Sure, they traded for Tarik Skubal, but the operation looked faulty. With the returns of Sasaki, Pages, and Ohtani likely on Wednesday, they are finally reaching a level of healthy they haven't had for most of the season.
In other words, despite how uneven things have looked, the Dodgers are once again in a position to do whay they do best and flip the swith on during the month of October.

Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan sent a message to the team ahead of the postseason with his role on the team still uncertain.
Sheehan went to the minors at the beginning of August following the arrival of Tarik Skubal and a string of poor results on his part. Prior to his stint in the minors, Sheehan had a 5.29 ERA and had just allowed five earned runs in just 2.2 innings pitched.
How Long Was Emmet Sheehan in the Minors?
He managed to get right in the minors, though, allowing just three earned runs over the course of 18 innings pitched in Triple-A. He returned in the middle of September, and has three starts under his belt since returning.
In those appearances, Sheehan has a 0.53 ERA over the course of 17 innings pitched, striking out 24 batters. He pitched Sunday, striking out nine batters through 5.1 scoreless innings of relief, during which he only allowed one hit and one walk. On the year, Sheehan now has a 4.57 ERA through 112.1 innings pitched, striking out 132 batters during his time in MLB.
The Dodgers are optioning him back to Triple-A to keep their bullpen fresh throughout the remainder of the season as they look to secure the No. 2 seed in the NL, but he can still feature in the postseason and is willing to do whatever it takes to help the team.
“I feel like I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan told Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez and reporters. “Whatever role they want me to do going forward, I’m ready to do it. It was nice to get that experience coming out of the pen, and I’m ready to go.”
What Role Would Emmet Sheehan Have in the Postseason?
Sheehan has predominantly played as a starter for the Dodgers this season, making his first relief appearance of the year on Sunday, but would almost definitely stay in the bullpen if he makes the roster come October.
The Dodgers have a four-man rotation planned out already, as Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Skubal are all healthy and likely to be the Dodgers’ starters during the postseason.
Sheehan would fit in the bullpen as a long relief arm, and would likely be the Dodgers’ go-to man in those scenarios.
Landon Knack and Bobby Miller have taken on those responsibilities as of late, but Sheehan’s recent results should qualify him for a spot over both Knack and Miller.
Will the Dodgers Bring Emmet Sheehan to the Postseason?
The Dodgers are allowed a maximum of 13 pitchers on their roster for the postseason, and Sheehan will almost certainly be included in those options due to his ability to pitch out of the bullpen.
Sheehan came out of the bullpen for the Dodgers during last year’s postseason, and while he wasn’t the most effective in that role, his recent surge and experience in that area will be key for LA as they look to win a third consecutive World Series.
The right-hander won’t pitch again for the Dodgers in the regular season due to the minimum 15-day stay in the minors, so unless the Dodgers need to recall him due to an injury, he’ll hope the impression he made during his strong September is enough to warrant a spot on the postseason roster.

LOS ANGELES — Matt Wilkinson’s role has been nebulous during his short time in the majors. In his debut, he was an opener. On some days, he’s made traditional starts. In others, he’s been a multi-inning reliever.
Wilkinson is one of several young, inexperienced pitchers on this roster trying to prove he can start at the major-league level. His performance on Sunday afternoon at Dodger Stadium helped those efforts.
“Tugboat” couldn’t prevent the Giants, who lost 3-1 to the Dodgers, from being swept, but the rookie turned in arguably the best start of his short career. In his seventh career appearance, Wilkinson tossed five shutout innings against the NL West champions, collecting a career-high six strikeouts without recording a single walk.
“He was outstanding,” said manager Tony Vitello. “Back at it on the starting deal. To be honest with you, didn’t have a whole lot of trouble to navigate because of how well he threw the ball. … When there was potential for things brewing, he put an end to it.”
“Best one yet since being up,” Wilkinson said. “Really was just throwing all four pitches for strikes today, and that was kind of the mindset going into today. Compete with all four pitches, and I felt like I did a good job with that today.”
Vitello said it’s “too early” to know how Wilkinson could fit into next year’s pitching plans but assessed that Wilkinson is “pretty flexible.” Before Sunday, Wilkinson had pitched five scoreless innings with four strikeouts over his last two outings as a multi-inning reliever. When asked if he prefers starting or relieving, the 23-year-old responded he’s willing to pitch whatever role is needed.
“You want a guy that wants the ball and ain’t scared of those situations,” Vitello said.
Wilkinson certainly didn’t look scared in his first meeting with the reigning back-to-back World Series champions on their home turf. Even with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list and Kyle Tucker starting the day on the bench, the Dodgers’ lineup still featured future Hall of Famers Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman and multi-time All-Stars Max Muncy and Teoscar Hernández.
Against Wilkinson, that group couldn’t get anything cooking.
The only threats that the Dodgers posed against Wilkinson were one-out doubles in the second and fifth innings. On both occasions, Wilkinson maneuvered out of trouble and completed five innings for just the second time in his career.
“Especially with this rivalry, it’s awesome and fun to be a small piece of that,” Wilkinson said.
Despite Wilkinson’s efforts, the Dodgers generated enough offense after his departure to complete the dusting.
Tommy Edman tied the game in the bottom of the sixth by turning a 2-2 cutter from Carson Seymour into a solo homer, and Kiké Hernández drove in the go-ahead run in the bottom of the seventh. Muncy, a long-time Giants (64-92) foe, added an RBI single in the bottom of the eighth for insurance.
Jonah Cox, with the use of his elite speed, generated San Francisco’s lone run in the top of the first.
Cox began the afternoon with a leadoff walk, then scrambled to second when the Dodgers’ Jack Dreyer made an errant pickoff throw. Already in scoring position, Cox swiped third with ease, his 14th steal of the season, then scored on a single by Victor Bericoto.
Following Dreyer’s lone inning as the opener, San Francisco couldn’t generate any offense against Los Angeles’ Emmet Sheehan, who allowed one hit over 5 1/3 scoreless innings of long relief with nine strikeouts. Sheehan has been outstanding against the Giants in his career, allowing four runs over 33 1/3 innings
By afternoon’s end, the Giants were reduced to their most inexperienced, anonymous lineup of the season. Rookie Bryce Eldridge missed a third straight game due to a head laceration, and right fielder Jung Hoo Lee was lifted from the game after fouling a pitch off his groin in the top of the sixth. Eldridge is not expected to play on Monday.
Up next
The Giants will return to Oracle Park for their final six games of the regular season, beginning with a three-game set against the Minnesota Twins.

item.content:encoded:
With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres.
Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages, who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from it on Monday, an off day for the Dodgers and Padres. The two National League West rivals can each clinch something important at Dodger Stadium—a berth in the postseason for San Diego and a first-round bye for Los Angeles.
Sasaki posted a 3.05 ERA in seven starts after the All-Star break but developed a blister on his throwing hand in August. Pages played in his first All-Star Game in July but fractured a bone in his right hand when he was hit by a 100.2 mph fastball from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler on Aug. 21.
The Dodgers were able to clinch the National League West without the two players, but both figure to play key roles in October for the defending World Series champions.
Postseason roles
The team lost hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez to a back injury earlier this month. For all his second-half success as a starter, the Dodgers need Sasaki more in their bullpen as a right-handed complement to left-handers Tanner Scott and Alex Vesia.
Pages, meanwhile, was excelling at the plate and in the field prior to his injury, which required surgery. He’ll have six games to tune up for the postseason—and a chance at redemption for last October.
The Dodgers won the World Series even though Pages had only four hits in 16 postseason games, managing just an .078 batting average across four playoff rounds.
Without Pages, the Dodgers moved veteran utilityman Tommy Edman to center field. Through week’s end, he was slashing .245/.328/.376 (94 OPS+) in 79 games this season.
The Dodgers are also expecting Shohei Ohtani to return during the Padres series, but he isn’t eligible to be activated from the 15-day injured list before Wednesday.
In corresponding 26-man roster moves, pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.

item.content:encoded:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

item.content:encoded:
Roki Sasaki is among the players expected to rejoin the Los Angeles Dodgers this week as they inch closer to full strength ahead of the postseason.
The right-hander has been on the 15-day injured list since Aug. 27 due to a blister on his right middle finger, but made steady progress throughout his recovery. He has thrown multiple bullpen sessions and live batting practices this month, including 48 pitches over four innings last Wednesday.
Sasaki was originally slated to return as a starting pitcher, but he now appears headed to the bullpen for the remainder of the 2026 season. The 24-year-old is capable of pitching multiple innings as a reliever, but not in the traditional sense of a bulk pitcher.
“I can see multiples, but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings. It won’t be that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s role.
Sasaki won’t be limited to simply providing length out of the bullpen. Roberts also indicated that he would feel comfortable using him in high-leverage situations, but only at the start of a “clean inning.”
As for whether Sasaki could get save opportunities, it’s something that Roberts might consider down the road.
“It won’t be in the ninth the first time, but it potentially could fall out (that way),” the Dodgers skipper said.
Tanner Scott has been the Dodgers’ primary closer in recent weeks, but Edwin Díaz recently returned from the 15-day IL and is hoping to eventually reclaim the role. Edgardo Henriquez also received save opportunities prior to landing on the IL with lower back discomfort.
Roki Sasaki’s postseason success
Sasaki shined as a reliever during the Dodgers’ World Series run last year, pitching to a minuscule 0.84 ERA and 1.03 WHIP with three saves in nine appearances. His previous success on baseball’s biggest stage played a role in the team’s decision to once again move him to the bullpen.
“Yeah. He’s done it, he’s really good, he’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff,” Roberts said. “You really just need four starters, so we’re in a good spot there for now.”
Along with Sasaki, the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen could include other traditional starters such as Justin Wrobleski and Emmet Sheehan. The club’s starting rotation will feature two of the league’s best arms in Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal.

LOS ANGELES — Emmet Sheehan continued his late-season hot streak with another strong outing on Sunday against the San Francisco Giants, with nine strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings, allowing only a single and a walk.
“I’ve loved the version of Emmet we’ve seen the last three outings,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. “He’s been fantastic.”
Sheehan in three starts over the last two weeks since rejoining the Dodgers has allowed only one run in 17 innings, with 24 strikeouts against only three walks. It came after spending most of August in Triple-A.
“I don’t know if I proved anything to myself,” Sheehan said. “It was more just getting a couple of things right, and I’m in a much better spot now.”
Sheehan was in the Dodgers rotation from opening day through August 2, when he allowed three home runs and five runs in a loss to the Boston Red Sox. Twenty starts into the season, Sheehan wasn’t getting results (5.29 ERA, belying his 4.00 xERA), and was having issues holding his velocity throughout his starts. He was optioned to Oklahoma City the next day.
That time in the minors was productive for Sheehan. After a planned shortened outing in which he allowed two runs in 2/3 of an inning, Sheehan struck out 24 over three starts with one run allowed in 17 1/3 innings. That earned him a Pacific Coast League pitcher of the week award and pitcher of the month honors for August.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me, and I was going to get right,” Sheehan said. “I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here, so I needed that a little bit. I feel like in a good spot.”
“We’ve seen confidence. When you’re essentially fighting for your life, to create an opportunity for yourself, that’s what I see. There’s urgency,” Roberts said. “I like the way he’s trusting his stuff, he’s in a good spot physically, and the performance has been fantastic.”
One tweak Sheehan made was throwing his curveball more. In his last three outings with the Dodgers, he threw the curve 21.9 percent of the time, up from his 12.3 percent over the course of the season.
“It’s something, Connor [McGuiness, assistant pitching coach], Mark [Prior, pitching coach], and I and the coaches down at Triple-A have been working on a lot is expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “Some guys ended up throughout the season sitting more mid-speed, slider, changeup on me. I think having that change of speeds has been really important.
On Sunday against San Francisco, Sheehan induced 15 of his 18 swinging strikes on his fastball and curveball and finished off five of his nine strikeouts with those two pitches.
Sheehan’s first 26 outings this year were starts, but on Sunday he followed an opener, at the very least getting him oriented about his possible relief role in the postseason. After three solid months in the rotation last season, Sheehan pitched in relief in October, with mixed results (8.59 ERA, 13 hits and five walks in 7 1/3 innings). He allowed runs in each of his four appearances, though rebounded with 2 2/3 scoreless innings in extras in the marathon Game 3, when got three outs with two strikeouts in a scoreless outing in the seventh and eighth innings of Game 7.
“The routine of everything can be a little hard to adjust to, so having that experience helps a lot. Getting back into that, I know what I need to do to be ready to go in the game,” Sheehan said. “Execution was off in the first couple, but then I felt better as it went on.”
Sheehan returned Sunday when Tarik Skubal went on the bereavement list, and the plan is for Sheehan to be optioned back to Triple-A, perhaps as early as Tuesday when Roki Sasaki is likely activated from the injured list straight into a high-leverage relief role.
Roberts on Sunday said the plan is for Sheehan to start on Saturday in the Triple-A championship game, provided Oklahoma City beats Las Vegas in the best-of-3 PCL championship starting Tuesday. But after that, Sheehan will almost certainly be on the playoff roster. Most likely he’ll be in a relief role, but that might depend on how Blake Snell progresses over the next two weeks from his left groin tightness.
“After [Sheehan] makes that last start, we’ll evaluate where we are as a staff,” Roberts said.
“Whatever role they want me to do going forward, I’m ready to do it,” Sheehan said. “It was nice to get that experience coming out of the pen.”

Will Roki Sasaki again be the Dodgers’ closer in the playoffs?
The Dodgers have created a pathway to make that possible, as manager Dave Roberts said that Sasaki will be moved into the bullpen when he is activated from the injured list this week.
Sasaki has pitched in 23 games this season, every one of them starts. A blister on his pitching hand has sidelined him since Aug. 27, but Roberts said he expected him to be activated during an upcoming three-game series against the Padres that starts on Tuesday.
The Dodgers had refrained from turning Sasaki into a reliever up to this point because of concerns over their starting rotation. Blake Snell departed from his most recent start after one inning because of a tight groin, but the two-time Cy Young Award winner has since not experienced any problems in that area.
The team believes it has four healthy starters in Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow. Emmet Sheehan figures to be the rotation’s new insurance policy, as Sheehan has allowed only one run in 17 innings pitched this month.
Roberts said he doesn’t plan to use Sasaki as a quasi-starter who pitches four or five innings following an opener.
Asked if Sasaki would be used in late-inning, high-leverage situations, Roberts replied, “I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably start a clean inning, but, yeah.”
Could he close?
“It won’t be the ninth inning the first time,” Roberts said.
But Roberts acknowledged there was a chance Sasaki could end up in that role.
Sasaki became the Dodgers’ closer last year by default, as the team didn’t have any other options. He saved three games in the postseason.
His move to the bullpen last year came after he missed 4 ½ months because of shoulder problems. He agreed to try pitching in relief under the condition the Dodgers let him start again the next season.
Sasaki is 5-5 with a 4.70 earned-run average this year, but was 2-0 with a 3.05 ERA in the seven starts he made after the All-Star break.
The Dodgers started this season counting on $69-million free agent addition Edwin Diaz to be their closer, but the three-time All-Star has endured a nightmare of a season that has included two IL stints. In Diaz’s absence, Tanner Scott has served as the team’s primary ninth-inning option and has performed well. However, Scott has posted a 4.97 ERA over his last 14 games.

The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants.
They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League West title and 13 out of 14 on Thursday.
Entering the final week of the season, the Dodgers can clinch a bye week with a magic number of three over the Braves.
Batter of the week
Kyle Tucker is starting to turn things around at the plate, and followed up an excellent series the previous weekend in Miami with nine hits in 20 at-bats, with three home runs and two doubles, with six walks and just one strikeout.
Honorable mention goes to Mookie Betts, who tied a Dodgers record with three doubles on Saturday, part of a stretch of three consecutive games with at least three hits. Will Smith found his power again with two home runs and a double, and Alex Freeland reached base eight times in 14 trips to the plate, including a home run and a double.
Pitcher of the week
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Reds on Tuesday, his third straight seven-inning start in September. Yamamoto this season has allowed zero or one run in 14 of his 27 starts.
Honorable mention goes to Justin Wrobleski, who retired all nine batters he faced with three strikeouts while starting Thursday’s division clincher in Cincinnati, and to Landon Knack, who got the win in that game with four scoreless innings in relief. Also to Emmet Sheehan, who continued his strong six-week run with nine strikouts in 5 1/3 scoreless frames on Sunday.

Miscellany
Half a hundred: The Dodgers have won 10 games in a row at home, and Sunday’s win was their 50th win at Dodger Stadium this season. That’s six straight years with 50 wins at home, plus seven straight full seasons dating back to 2019. Since moving into Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers won 50 home games 12 times in 51 full seasons through 2014. But since 2015, they’ve won at least 50 games at home 10 times in 11 full seasons.
A crowded 10-K: Tyler Glasnow beat the Giants on Friday with a strong six innings, including 10 strikeouts. Glasnow is the eighth different Dodgers pitcher with a 10-strikeout game this season, the most in franchise history. No other MLB team this year has more than five such pitchers.
Parliamentary procedure: After making the All-Star team as a starter with the Kansas City Royals in 2025, left-hander Kris Bubic was on the 60-day injured list when the Dodgers acquired him just ahead of the August 3 trade deadline. Now he’s pitching in relief, angling for a spot on the postseason roster. With his appearance on Wednesday, Bubic became the 33rd different Dodgers pitcher used this season. So far, Bubic has four strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings in three appearances. “It’s just funk,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday of Bubic. “It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact. I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out. I like those converted starters, because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
A quirk: The division clincher Thursday in Cincinnati was an 8-2 win, then came four home runs in the eighth inning Friday on the 20th anniversary of the 4+1 Game for another 8-2 triumph. That was the first time in Dodgers history they’ve won consecutive games by an 8-2 score.
Transactions
Monday: The fresh arm express was busy this week, beginning with Emmet Sheehan getting optioned the day after pitching six scoreless innings, in favor of Paul Gervase.
Monday: One day after a rare bad outing, Edgardo Henriquez was placed on the injured list with low back discomfort, ending his regular season and putting his playoff availability in question. Bobby Miller returned from Triple-A.
Wednesday: Trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic was activated off the 60-day IL to make his Dodgers debut in relief, the team’s 33rd pitcher of the season. Gervase was optioned and Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Thursday: Miller was sent back to Oklahoma City, and Landon Knack was called up to pitch four scoreless innings in relief in the division clincher in Cincinnati.
Sunday: Sheehan got the call back up to the Dodgers, with Tarik Skubal placed on the bereavement list. Kyle Hurt was also called up, with Seth Halvorsen optioned.

The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, on Sunday and improved to 96-60 on the year. They completed the series sweep of the divisional rivals and notched their fourth-straight win (and 14th of the last 17).
After Jack Dreyer took the start and allowed an earned run in the first inning, Emmet Sheehan pitched the next 5.1 frames and stole the show on the mound. He struck out nine, allowed one hit, one walk and no earned runs.
Offensively, Teoscar Hernndez, Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy and Josue De Paula each had a two-hit game. De Paula was 5-for-10 over the course of the series, just the first of hopefully many more at Dodger Stadium.
Ahead of the eventual victory, southpaw Tarik Skubal unfortunately had to be placed on the bereavement list. As he deals with his personal matter, it is likely that he will still make one more start (he is next scheduled for Sept. 26) before the postseason.
In other news, manager Dave Roberts made a somewhat surprising admission regarding superstar Mookie Betts. After hitting just .235 before the All-Star break, Betts has completely turned things around and looks like a more familiar version of himself, hitting .322 in his last 30 games.
"I couldn't tell you that I saw this," Roberts said on Saturday regarding Betts' turnaround. "But I just felt that he was stronger. He's worked hard on that. He looks great. He's not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great."
Finally, a Dodgers pitcher was demoted as part of the four-player roster move made on Sunday. The right-hander has an impressive 1.32 ERA across 26 games (27.1 innings) at the Triple-A level, but in 11 appearances with the Dodgers this season, he has an 8.10 ERA across 10 innings of work.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

21 Sep 2026, 11:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Erik Williams)
Mike Yastrzemski capped a four-run sixth inning with a three-run homer, and the visiting Atlanta Braves clinched the National League East with a 4-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Sunday.
The Braves swept the three-game interleague series and claimed their seventh division pennant over the last nine seasons. Yastrzemski was the last of four batters to reach safely against Astros left-handed reliever Bryan King (3-6), who didn't record a single out and exited after allowing Yastrzemski's 12th homer of the season.
Jose Altuve and Yainer Diaz homered for the spiraling Astros, who will enter the final week of the regular season one game behind the Texas Rangers in the American League West.
Astros starter Hunter Brown allowed just three singles and two walks over five shutout innings. Braves starter Martin Perez navigated traffic, allowing just one run on six hits and two walks in 4 1/3 innings.
Rays 5, Red Sox 1
Tampa Bay's Jonny DeLuca and Chandler Simpson drove in two runs apiece during a four-run first inning, Victor Mesa Jr. homered and the Rays defeated visiting Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla.
With the win, the Rays completed their final regular-season homestand with an 8-1 record and wrapped their home schedule with a major league-best 55-26 mark.
Trevor Story homered, and Roman Anthony and Caleb Durbin each went 2-for-4 for the Red Sox, who managed just six hits while losing their second straight game.
Pirates 4, Royals 3
Rafael Flores Jr. belted a go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth inning to cap Pittsburgh's three-game sweep over visiting Kansas City. With the win, the Pirates improved to 14-6 in their last 20 games.
Oneil Cruz went deep to lead off the fourth inning and Spencer Horwitz had an RBI single in the sixth for Pittsburgh. Carmen Mlodzinski earned the win after allowing two runs on three hits in three innings.
Vinnie Pasquantino had a pinch-hit two-run homer for the Royals, who have lost four in a row and seven of their past eight games.
Phillies 7, Mets 2
Cristopher Sanchez tossed 6 1/3 solid innings and earned the victory for visiting Philadelphia, which earned a much-needed win over New York.
Luis Arraez was 1-for-4 with two RBIs for the Phillies. Justin Crawford provided insurance in the eighth with a bases-clearing triple off Kodai Senga. Sanchez (18-6) gave up two runs on six hits. Philadelphia sits four games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks in the race for the final National League wild card.
Bo Bichette homered for the Mets, who dropped their home finale for the third time in four years, while Brett Baty had a pinch-hit run-scoring single in the seventh. Francisco Alvarez and A.J. Ewing each singled twice.
Cubs 9, Reds 1
Pete Crow-Armstrong tied the major league lead with his 45th home run, and David Peterson held host Cincinnati to one run on three hits in six innings in Chicago's win.
Crow-Armstrong was 3-for-5 with two RBIs, three runs, his 30th double and his 38th stolen base. He matched Philadelphia's Kyle Schwarber at 45 homers, and he became the first center fielder in history with 40 home runs, 30 doubles and 30 steals in a season.
Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered for the Cubs. JJ Bleday hit a home run for the Reds, who have dropped three of four.
Cardinals 5, Nationals 3
Leo Bernal's two-run home run capped a three-run eighth inning, and St. Louis rallied for a win against visiting Washington to salvage the finale of the three-game series.
Ivan Herrera tied it 3-3 with one out when he hit his second solo homer of the day. Luis Gastelum (5-3) pitched a scoreless inning for the win. Jose Fermin had two hits for the Cardinals, who had lost four straight.
CJ Abrams homered, and Daylen Lile had a double and a single for Washington, which had won six of seven.
Mariners 2, Rockies 1
Kade Anderson threw seven scoreless innings, allowing just three hits in the longest outing of his rookie season, and visiting Seattle stayed alive in the postseason race with a win over Colorado in Denver.
Dominic Canzone had two hits and two RBIs for Seattle, which gained a game on the Texas Rangers in the AL West. Closer Andres Munoz left the game in the ninth with an apparent right arm injury.
Hunter Goodman's 39th home run of the season couldn't prevent Colorado from moving within one loss of its fourth consecutive 100-loss season.
Blue Jays 7, Rangers 2
Nathan Lukes and Charles McAdoo each had two RBIs to lead Toronto to a win over Texas in Arlington, Texas.
Kazuma Okamoto broke a 2-2 deadlock with an RBI single in the fifth and gave the Blue Jays a lead they would never relinquish as they remained three games back of the final AL wild-card spot. Spencer Arrighetti (9-9) picked up the win, allowing two runs in 2 1/3 innings during a bullpen game.
Jake Burger delivered the Rangers' lone runs on a game-tying two-run homer in the fourth. Jacob deGrom (11-10) had a shaky outing, giving up three runs with five hits in 4 1/3 innings for Texas, which maintained its one-game lead in the AL West despite the defeat.
Brewers 3, Orioles 0
Jacob Misiorowski set the tone with three shutout innings and Milwaukee blanked host Baltimore for the second game in a row to complete a three-game sweep and set a franchise record for regular-season victories.
William Contreras homered, and Cooper Pratt provided two run-scoring singles with two outs. Milwaukee is two games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best record in the National League. Misiorowski's ERA dipped to 1.86.
The Orioles further damaged their fading playoff hopes, losing the first three games of the homestand to fall five games back of the Chicago White Sox for the final American League wild-card spot. Colton Cowser had two of Baltimore's four hits. Orioles starter Brandon Young (9-5) was charged with two runs in six innings.
Diamondbacks 8, Yankees 4
Nolan Arenado hit his third grand slam of the season to cap a five-run fifth and Arizona kept its slim National League wild-card chances alive with a victory over New York in Phoenix.
Geraldo Perdomo had two hits and two RBIs and five Arizona relievers limited the Yankees to three hits in 6 1/3 scoreless innings. The D-backs remained five games behind NL wild-card leaders Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres and four behind the Philadelphia Phillies with six to play.
Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones homered for the Yankees, who fell six games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East. The Yankees lead the American League with 216 homers. Lombard had two hits.
Twins 8, Angels 0
Dean Kremer allowed one hit over six innings and Alan Roden went 3-for-5 with a home run and four RBIs as Minnesota earned a split of its four-game series with Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif.
Josh Bell had three hits, a walk, two RBIs and a run while Brooks Lee also had three hits and scored three times for Minnesota, which finished with 13 hits. Kremer (4-5) allowed just a fourth-inning leadoff single to Vaughn Grissom.
Ryan Johnson (5-9) suffered the loss for Los Angeles, which finished the 2026 season with a 34-47 home record.
Guardians 1, Athletics 0
Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings to lift Cleveland past the visiting Athletics.
Williams (14-8) gave up only three hits while throwing 63 of 89 pitches for strikes. Steven Kwan had three hits and Cade Smith earned his 39th save as the Guardians swept the series and remain atop the American League Central.
A's starter Jack Perkins (3-12) gave up five hits and one run in six innings. Zack Gelof had two of the team's six hits as the Athletics suffered their sixth straight loss
Dodgers 3, Giants 1
Emmet Sheehan pitched brilliantly in long relief, Enrique Hernandez broke a seventh-inning tie with a run-scoring double and Los Angeles completed a three-game sweep of visiting San Francisco.
Tommy Edman homered for the Dodgers, who trailed 1-0 after one inning before Sheehan took over to start the second and held the Giants to just one hit with nine strikeouts over the next 5 1/3 scoreless innings.
Jung Hoo Lee and Victor Bericoto singled for the only hits for the Giants, who completed their road schedule with a 28-53 record. Sam Hentges (1-7) allowed a pair of one-out singles in the seventh before Hernandez's double for a 2-1 edge.
Padres 7, Marlins 3
Jake Cronenworth homered twice and knocked in a season-high five runs while Fernando Tatis Jr. also homered as host San Diego polished off a three-game sweep and finished 6-0 against Miami this season.
The Padres won their fifth straight game and are 13-1 in their last 14 games. Walker Buehler (9-6) worked 6 2/3 innings, allowing three hits and three runs.
Sandy Alcantara (13-11) absorbed the loss for the Marlins after permitting eight hits and four runs over six innings. Alcantara is winless in his last eight starts.
White Sox 8, Tigers 1
Chase Meidroth hit a two-run homer for Chicago and Sam Antonacci's two-run double highlighted a 2-for-4 performance as the White Sox waited through a rain delay of nearly four hours and played in wet, blustery conditions to beat Detroit.
Five pitchers held the Tigers to six hits and five walks as Detroit was limited to a single run for the third time in the series. Huascar Brazoban (6-2), reinstated prior to the game from the 15-day injured list (left lat strain), pitched for the first time since Aug. 24. He allowed a hit in one inning to get his first victory with the White Sox.
Tigers starter Troy Melton (8-5) allowed four runs in 3 2/3 innings, giving up four hits before exiting with a trainer. Detroit pitchers allowed eight walks, with White Sox third baseman Miguel Vargas (1-for-2) drawing three of them. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece.
Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep.
Sheehan retired 16 of the 18 batters he faced, allowing just one single and walking one while striking out nine.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.
“We’ve seen confidence. We’ve seen when you’re essentially fighting for your life to create an opportunity for yourself. That’s what I see. There’s urgency. I like the way that he’s trusting his stuff. He’s in a good spot physically, and you know the performance has been fantastic.”
The outing was Sheehan’s third consecutive outstanding performance this month as he has bounced between Triple-A and the majors. It cemented a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen after a rough season for the 26-year-old right-hander – an outcome that did not seem likely when he was demoted to Triple-A in early August.
“I don’t know that I proved anything to myself. It was just getting a couple things right and I think I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan said.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me and I was going to get right. I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here so I needed that a little bit.”
Sheehan has been called up for two starts this month and pitched in ‘bulk’ following Jack Dreyer as an opener on Sunday. Sheehan carried a 5.29 ERA into September after 20 starts for the Dodgers that landed him back in the minors.
In his three September outings, though, Sheehan has shown rediscovered fastball command after working on his delivery in Triple-A. He has allowed just one run in 17 innings, holding hitters to a .105 average (6 for 57) with 24 strikeouts and three walks. After giving up 20 home runs in those first 20 starts, he has allowed just one in his 17 September innings.
If his confidence didn’t need repair, his delivery and pitch mix needed some work.
Now two years removed from Tommy John surgery, Sheehan was thrown by not quite having recovered all of his fastball velocity this year. When he chased those extra miles per hour, it was counterproductive. He has become more comfortable at 94-95 mph now.
“I think it’s a few things,” he said Sunday. “Definitely … being more comfortable in my delivery, being out there staying free and easy with everything, not trying to do too much. Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 here.’ It’s more like ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it.’”
They haven’t. Sheehan has gotten 50 swings-and-misses in his three outings this month, nearly half of them (24) on his reborn four-seam fastball. He also got six on his curveball on Sunday.
“That’s something that (assistant pitching coach) Connor (McGuinness), (pitching coach) Mark (Prior) and I and the coaches down in Triple-A have been working on is just expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “I think some guys ended up throughout the season sitting mid-speed, slider-changeup, on me. Having that change of speeds the last couple has been very important.”
The Dodgers moved Sheehan to the bullpen for the postseason last October and saw him as a big weapon in that role. The results were mixed, however, in part because of some pitch tipping issues which Sheehan said have been addressed. He will be wiser this time around, he said.
“Definitely,” Sheehan said. “I think the routine of everything can be a little bit hard to adjust to right away. So having that experience helps a lot. Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game.”
The Dodgers gave him a little bit of a test drive by using Dreyer as an ‘opener’ before him. The Giants scratched out one run in the first inning against Dreyer when he walked leadoff man Jonah Cox. Cox moved to second base on a wild pickoff attempt by Dreyer, stole third and scored on Victor Bericoto’s RBI single. The Giants had just one more hit in the game.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94-95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who will rejoin Oklahoma City for the Triple-A playoffs this week before returning to the Dodgers for the postseason. “That’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it 85 pitches.”
The Giants’ run against Dreyer stood up as the only run of the day until Tommy Edman emerged from a 2-for-41 slump to hit a solo home run in the sixth inning.
The Dodgers broke the 1-1 tie in the seventh on singles by Max Muncy and Josue De Paula followed by an RBI double from Kiké Hernandez.
They stranded De Paula and Hernandez in scoring position, but singles by Teoscar Hernandez, Freddie Freeman and Muncy produced another run in the eighth inning.
Kris Bubic, Brock Stewart and Tanner Scott combined on 2⅔ innings of hitless relief to close out the combined two-hitter for the Dodgers’ 96th win. With the win, the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Atlanta Braves (who clinched the National League East division title on Sunday) dropped to three with six games left in the regular season.
The Dodgers (96-60) remain two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (98-58) for the top seed, though the Brewers also hold the head-to-head tiebreaker. The No. 3 seed – currently Atlanta (92-64) – will play host to a best-of-three Wild Card Series against either the Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) or Philadelphia Phillies (86-70).

item.content:encoded:
Emmet Sheehan’s next start will be in the minor leagues.
The right-hander might be out of sight, but that doesn’t mean he will be out of mind.
His scheduled start Saturday for triple-A Oklahoma City in a Pacific Coast League playoff game is part of a design to prepare him to pitch for the Dodgers in October.
Sheehan has pitched his way into consideration for a spot on the playoff roster.
His quote-unquote demotion came after he pitched 5 ⅓ scoreless innings in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ sweep-sealing 3–1 victory over the San Francisco Giants Sunday.
The game was the third Sheehan pitched this month for the Dodgers. His numbers in those three games: 17 innings pitched, one run allowed, 24 strikeouts, three walks.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.”
Sent down to Oklahoma City in early August, Sheehan returned to the major leagues earlier this month with a slightly modified arsenal that has significantly improved his results. He’s thrown his curveball more, and his increased inability to change speeds has made his fastball play up even when he’s not touching 97 mph with it.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94–95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said. “So I think that’s something that, that’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it, 85 pitches.”
With the Dodgers expecting to start Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow in the postseason, the team has started the process of moving Sheehan into a relief role by having Jack Dreyer pitch an inning as opener Sunday. Sheehan was down in triple-A over the last week but a roster spot for him was opened up because Skubal went on the bereavement list.
Sheehan entered the game in the second inning and pitched into the seventh. He gave up only one hit and one walk; he struck out nine.
He said he has made it a point to feel “free and easy” with his delivery.
“Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 [mph] here,’ it’s more like, ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it,’” Sheehan said.
What it means
The teams with the two-best records in each league will earn a first-round bye and the Dodgers are close to wrapping up one of those spots. With their win over the Giants, the Dodgers maintained a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the National League’s No. 2 seed. Both teams have only six games remaining in the regular season.
Who’s hot
Left-hander Kris Bubic, who was acquired from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline, replaced Sheehan in the seventh inning and registered the final two outs of the inning. Bubic struck out Scott Bandura, only for Shay Whitcomb to reach base on a throwing error by Max Muncy.
No problem: Bubic forced Grant McCray to fly out to left field.
Bubic has pitched 2 ⅔ innings in three appearances for the Dodgers over the last week, and he still hasn’t allowed a run. He has struck out four.
Roberts said he’s also pitched his way into consideration for a spot on the playoff roster.
“It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact,” Roberts said. “I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out, and I like those converted starters because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
Who’s Not
For today, this section should be renamed “Who Wasn’t Hot.”
The label certainly applied to Tommy Edman, who was two for his last 42 before his sixth-inning at-bat: That’s when Edman jumped on an inside cutter from Carson Seymour and launched it into the visiting bullpen behind the right-field wall.
Edman’s home run tied the game at 1–1.
Up next
The Dodgers have a day off Monday. They will resume play Tuesday when they host the San Diego Padres, who will send No. 1 starter Michael King (12-9, 3.03 ERA) to the mound. The Dodgers won’t have a traditional starter, as Roberts said the team is planning for a bullpen game.

Por DAN GREENSPAN
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Kiké Hernández conectó un doble productor que puso a su equipo por delante en la séptima entrada, Emmet Sheehan no permitió carreras en 5 1/3 innings, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron 3-1 a los Gigantes de San Francisco el domingo para completar una barrida de tres juegos.
El boricua Hernández atacó el primer lanzamiento que vio de Sam Hentges (1-7) e impulsó a Max Muncy para poner a los Dodgers arriba 2-1. Muncy añadió una carrera de seguridad con un sencillo en la octava.
Kris Bubic (4-2) lanzó 2/3 de inning para llevarse la victoria, y Tanner Scott se encargó de la novena entrada para su 23er salvamento.
Sheehan aprovechó al máximo un juego de bullpen para reforzar sus credenciales de cara a integrar el roster de postemporada de los Dodgers como relevista largo. Ponchó a nueve, permitió un hit y otorgó una base por bolas después de relevar a Jack Dreyer en la segunda entrada.
Matt Wilkinson permitió tres hits y no dio bases por bolas, además de ponchar a seis en cinco episodios sin permitir carreras, pero el bullpen de los Gigantes se vino abajo. El zurdo de 23 años fue adquirido como parte del canje que envió al receptor Patrick Bailey a Cleveland en mayo.
Tommy Edman conectó un jonrón hacia el jardín derecho en la sexta entrada para empatar el juego 1-1, castigando al relevista Carson Seymour con un batazo de 400 pies.
Jonah Cox recibió una base por bolas abriendo la entrada para ayudar a que los Gigantes tomaran ventaja 1-0. Cox llegó a segunda por un mal intento de sorprenderlo en la inicial por parte de Dreyer antes de robarse la tercera, y un sencillo de Victor Bericoto lo remolcó.
